RoomType.rationale: TheLostAndForgottenNormal declares RoomType.Monster; the bucket-membership counterpart agrees.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: C# declares the 2-element array [TheLost, TheForgotten] (Queen-style array literal, ModelDb.Monster<TheLost>() first). The sim's monster_classes carries the same two classes. AllPossibleMonsters is an unordered superset used for previews/asset-preload, not a placement list, so the two sides agreeing as a SET (order immaterial here) is the right bar; both are also the fixed, always-spawning roster so there is no possible divergence.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: C#'s GenerateMonsters returns (TheLost, null) then (TheForgotten, null), in that order -- exactly TheLostAndForgottenNormal's own AllPossibleMonsters order. Sim's monster_classes = [TheLost, TheForgotten], same order, and create_monsters constructs `[cls(hooks, rng) for cls in monster_classes]`, preserving it into combat.enemies. Neither tuple carries a slot name (both null / monster_slots left at its default empty tuple, so slot_name stays None on both created creatures). Zero RNG draws in GenerateMonsters on either side -- neither TheLost nor TheForgotten's constructor consumes the per-encounter Rng (their own Possess-Strength/-Speed powers and move machines are monster-tier, not encounter-tier, concerns). Roster, order, slot and draw-count all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: the Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) is never registered as a hook listener; only Monster instances register themselves
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: Same structural fact as every unit in this batch.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward -- not overridden, inherits the Monster ladder (10-20) x Poverty multiplier
guards.rationale: sts2_rl/rewards.py GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER] = (10, 20) and THE_LOST_AND_FORGOTTEN_NORMAL sets neither min_gold nor max_gold -- matches. Poverty/ascension scaling out of scope per PROMPT.md, and not modelled by rewards.py.

guards.what: ShouldGiveRewards / IsWeak -- neither overridden, both default (true / false)
guards.rationale: Encounter.should_give_rewards defaults True and is unset here; the_lost_and_forgotten appears only in normal_keys, matching IsWeak's inherited false.
